title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1, plus a less-restricted version for security and science experts
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, which it calls its most advanced model for coding and knowledge work, through its API and the major cloud platforms. Alongside it came Claude Mythos 5.1: the same model, but with different safeguards, so it holds back less on cybersecurity and life-sciences work. Mythos is only available to a set of vetted US organizations in Anthropic's verification programs.
why_it_matters: Instead of one set of rules for everyone, checked experts doing defensive security or scientific research get a version that holds back less in their field.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, built to do whole tasks on a computer
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, which it calls its most intelligent model and its best yet at alignment, meaning doing what people actually intend. OpenAI says its biggest strength is computer use: operating a browser and apps to handle tasks like filling out online forms, updating customer records, and organizing a calendar. It rolled out first to a limited set of organizations, with paid ChatGPT plans, OpenAI's API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock to follow over the next few days.
why_it_matters: OpenAI is pitching Astra as something you can hand whole tasks to, not just questions. If it works as described, it could take over tedious computer chores that people do every day.

title: Google DeepMind maps what every possible single-letter DNA change might do
summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, a collection of predictions from its AlphaGenome AI model for all 9 billion possible single-letter changes in human DNA, showing how each one might affect the way cells work. It also covers the 98% of DNA that doesn't directly hold instructions for proteins, which is much harder to study. Academic researchers can search it free on a website, and Google says commercial use through Google Cloud is coming soon.
why_it_matters: A ready-made map of what each DNA change might do could help researchers track down the genetic cause of rare diseases that doctors haven't been able to explain.

title: Grok 4.7 aims at coding and office work for a low price
summary: SpaceXAI, the company formerly called xAI, released Grok 4.7, its most capable model for coding and knowledge work. It's built on a new, larger base model and was trained to keep working longer on hard tasks and to check its own work more carefully. It costs the same as Grok 4.6, starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, and it's available in Cursor, Grok Build, and the Grok API.
why_it_matters: By xAI's own price comparison, that's much cheaper than many competing top models, which makes Grok 4.7 a budget option for heavy coding work.

title: Claude helps discover a new enzyme system with CRISPR-like DNA patterns
summary: Scientists prompted Claude to search a huge database of DNA for new examples of one type of enzyme. About 950 Claude agents worked for 21 hours, narrowed more than 200,000 candidates down to 20, and spotted an unusual one in viruses that infect bacteria: an enzyme next to a pattern of repeating DNA similar to CRISPR, the bacterial system scientists turned into a gene-editing tool. Early tests in Anthropic's lab showed the system is switched on, but what it actually does is still unknown.
why_it_matters: It's an example of AI agents doing a real piece of scientific discovery, from searching the data to finding something new, with scientists testing the result.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5, faster and cheaper per task than Sonnet 5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5, a model aimed at everyday work like fixing bugs and writing polished documents. Anthropic says it writes its answers more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less per task, even though the price per token hasn't changed. It's available in the Claude web app, Claude Code, Anthropic's API, and the major cloud platforms.
why_it_matters: The same work gets done faster and for less money. For businesses that run Claude on a lot of tasks, up to 30% less per task adds up.

title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol promises near-Astra skill at a fifth of the price
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol, an upgrade to its GPT-6 Sol model. OpenAI says it comes close to its top model, GPT-6 Astra, on coding, computer use, and professional work, while costing developers one-fifth as much. It's available on paid ChatGPT plans in ChatGPT Work and Codex and to developers through the API, but not yet in regular ChatGPT chat.
why_it_matters: Price matters as much as power. A model that's nearly as capable at a fraction of the cost makes running AI agents affordable for more businesses.

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon, starting with cybersecurity defenders
summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier model, built for complex software engineering, legal and finance work, and cybersecurity defense. It can write up to 1 million tokens in a single response, up from 64,000. Google is releasing it in stages, starting with trusted cybersecurity defenders in its Fairwind program, then paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers, with wider access to follow.
why_it_matters: This is Google's next big model generation, but most people won't be able to use it right away because of the staged rollout.
